evals.prompt: skipshare init  (machine has Node v18, no SkipShare CLI, Homebrew installed)
evals.expected_output: Checks first, then one confirm listing the Node.js update, the CLI install and the login, and waits for ok. Nothing is installed yet.
expectations: Runs `node -v` and checks for the `skipshare` command before replying
Shows one list that mentions updating Node.js (v18 is older than 20), installing the SkipShare CLI and logging in
Ends with `Reply **ok** to start, or **N** to cancel.`
Runs no install command (`brew`, `npm install`, `nvm`, `winget`) before the user replies ok

evals.prompt: ok  (after the setup confirm; Node v18 from Homebrew, no CLI; login status error.data.token_page_url is https://app.example.com/settings/access-tokens)
evals.expected_output: Upgrades Node.js with brew, installs the CLI globally, then asks the user to create and copy a token without pasting it.
expectations: Runs `brew upgrade node` (or `brew install node`) and checks `node -v` again
Runs `npm install -g https://te-fsharing-dev-cli.s3.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/skipshare-cli-latest.tgz` and never uses `sudo`
Gives the link https://app.example.com/settings/access-tokens to create a token and asks the user to reply **ok** after copying it
Says not to paste the token into the chat

evals.expected_output: Pipes the clipboard into `skipshare login --json` and reports the logged-in email.
expectations: Runs `pbpaste | skipshare login --json`
Never prints, echoes or saves the clipboard content
On exit 0 replies `✅ Logged in as` followed by the email
Then asks the language question as a numbered list with `1. English` and `2. 日本語 (Japanese)`

evals.prompt: ok  (login with the clipboard token exits 3: token rejected)
evals.expected_output: Short invalid-token error asking to copy the token again and reply ok. No token requested in chat.
expectations: Output starts with `❌ That token isn't valid.`
Asks the user to copy the whole token again (or create a new one) and reply **ok**
Does not ask the user to paste the token into the chat

evals.prompt: skipshare init  (Node missing, no brew, nvm or winget)
evals.expected_output: After ok, cannot install Node.js: points to nodejs.org and waits for retry.
expectations: Does not run `sudo` or ask for a password
Shows `❌ I can't install Node.js here.` with the https://nodejs.org link
Ends with reply **retry**

evals.expected_output: Stops without sudo and asks the user to fix the npm prefix, then retry.
expectations: Does not retry with `sudo`
Does not fall back to `npx`
Links the npm EACCES guide and waits for **retry**

evals.prompt: 2  (answer to the language question; team list has the user's own team plus Acme owned by boss@acme.com)
evals.expected_output: Sets Japanese, then asks the default-team question in Japanese with the personal team first.
expectations: Runs `config language ja --json`
The following reply is in Japanese
The team list starts with `1.` for the personal team and lists `Acme (boss@acme.com)`
Does not list the row whose `role` is `owner` as a separate team
Mentions **skip** to keep the personal team

evals.prompt: 2  (answer to the default-team question; option 2 is Acme, boss@acme.com)
evals.expected_output: Sets the default team, shows the ready summary and send examples.
expectations: Runs `config default-team boss@acme.com --json`
Shows `✅ SkipShare is ready.` with the account, language and default team
Gives two or three example send requests

evals.prompt: set up SkipShare  (Node v22, CLI installed, already logged in as me@example.com)
evals.expected_output: No install confirm. Says it is already set up and goes to the settings.
expectations: Does not show the install confirm or run any install command
Says SkipShare is already set up as me@example.com
Goes on to the language question

evals.prompt: ok  (token copied, but no clipboard tool works in this environment)
evals.expected_output: Asks the user to run the login in their own terminal and reply ok, then checks login status.
expectations: Asks the user to run `skipshare login` in their own terminal and paste the token at the hidden prompt
Does not ask for the token in the chat
After the next ok, runs `login status --json`
